### Shipping

**You own what lands. Verify each PR independently, land only the verified run from the root, then keep your hands off the stack.**

Use the forge CLI, `gh` for GitHub or `glab` for GitLab, read from the repository's remote. In T3 Code, use its pull request tools instead where they are listed, and pass the head SHA the verdict covers to every merge ([t3-code.md](../references/harnesses/t3-code.md#pull-requests)). Never require Graphite (`gt`).

1. **Verify each PR independently before it lands.** One verifier per PR, a `go-worker` subagent on `small` that did not write the code, runs the change the way a user would through the **control-ui** or **control-cli** skill, parent against head, and posts `PASS`, `PASS+NOTES`, or `FAIL` on that PR with the SHA it ran. Only a verdict from an agent that did not write the code counts, because an author checks what it meant to build. Green CI and an approving bot review are not verdicts, because neither runs the change as a user would.
2. **Land only the contiguous verified run rooted at the bottom.** Walk up from the lowest unmerged PR and stop at the first one without `PASS` or `PASS+NOTES`. The PRs below it are the run, and the top one is the ceiling. A verified PR above an unverified one waits, because it cannot land without the code below it. One whose branch neither holds nor needs that code can move onto trunk and land on its own. It needs a fresh verdict first, because its old one ran with that code beneath it and trunk does not have it.
3. **Re-check that the verdicts still describe the code.** A verdict covers a patch, and a chain rebase moves every PR above it to a new SHA without failing any check. Each verdict records the base SHA and head SHA it ran on. Before trusting an older verdict, run [`scripts/same-patch.sh`](../scripts/same-patch.sh)` <verdict-base> <verdict-head> <current-base> <current-head>`. It compares the whole PR's patch from its merge base, whitespace and binary files included, so trunk moving on doesn't change it, while a change to any commit does, even under the same tip. It prints `same` (exit 0) or `differs` (exit 1). Exit 2 is an error, such as an unknown commit, and never counts as the same. When the patches differ only in tests, docs, or lint config, a lane's result stands if what it ran builds the same at both SHAs apart from noise. Noise is a difference that also shows up between two builds of the verdict SHA, or an embedded commit SHA. Report each kind of noise with its files, so a reader can check the call. The change itself still gets fresh checks and a review, because the old verdict never saw it. A lane with no build output, such as a dev server, cannot show this, so rerun it, and re-verify anything else that drifted.
4. **Land bottom-up, one PR at a time.** Always merge the run's lowest unmerged PR, pinned to its current head once the verdict covers that head, either directly or carried forward by step 3 (`gh pr merge <pr> --squash --match-head-commit <sha>` or `glab mr merge <mr> --squash --sha <sha> --yes`), so the forge refuses a head that moved. A PR whose base is still its parent's branch merges into that branch, not trunk. Read the PR back for the result (`gh pr view <pr> --json state,mergedAt,baseRefName`), because a merge command can report success when a merge queue only queued the PR, and a requested auto-merge is not a merge. A landed PR reads merged with trunk as its base, not its parent's branch. Arm auto-merge only on a PR whose verdict covers its current head, because it lands whatever head is ready. After a merge lands, retarget the PR whose base was the merged branch to trunk (`gh pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>`), move its patch onto the merge result, and push with `--force-with-lease`. The verdict covers the patch, not its commits, so step 3's patch-id rule decides whether the verdict survives. Merge it once its checks pass and its verdict survives.
5. **Leave the stack alone while it lands.** Step 4's move of the next PR is the only change to a branch or base, because a merge lands whatever its branch and base hold at that moment, verdict or not. Wait on each merge the way the **Babysit** playbook waits. In T3 Code, when its PR watch tool is listed and Babysit's watch conditions hold, watch the run's PRs and end your turn, and read each PR back when a merge or check wakes you. Otherwise report each PR's state and hand back. Outside T3 Code, when checks are what blocks, run `gh pr checks <pr> --watch`, or `glab ci status --live` on the MR's branch, in the background and read the PR back each time it returns, until the ceiling reads merged. That wait sees checks only, not a review or a merge queue, so when one of those blocks, report the PR's state and stop. A base that moves to trunk when its parent merges is expected, not damage to repair. If a merge stalls, find out why before you change anything.
6. **Stop at the ceiling.** Extending the run takes new verdicts, so it is a new pass through step 1.

**Reply:** the verified run and its ceiling, each PR's verdict and who produced it, what landed and how you confirmed it, and what the next gap needs.
